items.title: AAM sounds alarm on ‘unsustainable, race to the bottom’ for generics and biosimilars
items.snippet: After years of price pressures, the trade group argues “the economics of generics have deteriorated to the point where sustainability of the industry is in peril.”

items.title: Report: The Insider's Guide to Thought Leadership in Biopharma
items.snippet: This guide explores the evolving role of podcasts, webinars, and thought leadership programs in biopharma and provides practical recommendations for public relations agencies, corporate communications teams, and commercial marketers looking to elevate their visibility and influence.

items.title: Summit, BioNTech, more headline WCLC with next-gen lung cancer drugs
items.snippet: BioNTech, Summit Therapeutics, GSK and Roche have made a splash at the ongoing World Conference on Lung Cancer taking place in South Korea. These companies and their partners have all shared new findings for their closely watched programs, highlighting overall survival benefits in various types of lung cancer.

items.title: Definium moves toward FDA submission for LSD drug in anxiety after ‘another clear win’
items.snippet: Positive topline results from a second straight study in generalized anxiety disorder shift the narrative for Definium Therapeutics’ DT120 to commercialization, Jefferies analysts said Monday, while Stifel wrote that the asset is moving towards an FDA submission.

items.title: Novo drops ‘Nordisk’ moniker, turns bull toward future in corporate rebrand
items.snippet: Analysts tentatively welcomed Novo’s new corporate rebrand—so long as it comes with a larger change to the company’s overall business strategy.

items.title: AstraZeneca’s newly approved cancer pill fails late-stage study, blocking path to bigger market
items.snippet: SERENA-4 was assessing AstraZeneca’s Etcamah as a first-line option for certain patients with advanced breast cancer—a setting that could have meant a $2.9 billion opportunity for the drug.

items.title: Scholar Rock secures first FDA approval for muscle-targeting rare disease drug
items.snippet: Scholar Rock’s spinal muscular atrophy drug, now to be called Isembyld, was originally rejected in September 2025, when the FDA cited compliance problems at a third-party manufacturer.

items.title: Cyclic peptides open new drug frontiers, if manufacturing can keep up
items.snippet: With oral cyclic peptides offering small molecule convenience and antibody‑like selectivity, the modality is gaining momentum. But bioavailability below 1%, minimal PK data and fragile synthesis still slow progress. Viva Biotech’s experts outlined how hybrid synthesis, ADME/PK modeling and AI‑guided design are expandi...

items.title: Unlocking cell surface protein research with site-specific labeling
items.snippet: Applications in flow cytometry, cell sorting, target validation, and therapeutic discovery

items.title: Psychedelic therapies ride wave of public favor into FDA hearing
items.snippet: Heading into an FDA hearing on Monday regarding the future of psychedelic treatments, public comments show wide support for further exploring the therapeutic potential of these compounds—to match rising support within the agency.

items.title: 5 drugmakers chasing Merck and Moderna in the cancer vaccine race
items.snippet: Following their blowout win in melanoma last month, Merck and Moderna are leading the way among a new crop of personalized cancer vaccines. Here are five companies with similar therapies hoping to break through where others have previously failed.

items.title: After a brief storm of political headwinds, mRNA is back with strong momentum
items.snippet: A year to the day after the Trump administration slashed $500 million in funding from mRNA-based programs, the FDA approved Moderna’s flu vaccine based on the technology. Weeks later, Moderna and Merck revealed positive Phase 3 results for their personalized mRNA-based cancer vaccine. In the words of one mRNA speciali...

items.snippet: Join BioSpace's Managing Editor, Director of Insights and Vice President of Marketing for an inside look at how PR, communications and marketing teams can successfully leverage webinars, podcasts and integrated content campaigns to elevate executive voices, share industry expertise and engage key biotech and pharma au...

items.title: Samsung Biologics inks $262M manufacturing deal with European pharma company
items.snippet: The agreement, which runs through 2033, comes as Samsung Biologics continues to expand its large manufacturing footprint in South Korea.

items.title: Disc sets up polycythemia vera challenge but Silence maintains lead
items.snippet: The polycythemia vera field is heating up, with Disc Medicine and Silence Therapeutics each advancing next-generation therapies, playing catch-up to Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics, who won the FDA’s approval last month for Mimrylo.

items.title: Frazier adds $1.1B+ to small and mid-sized biotech fund
items.snippet: Frazier’s life science fund has already benefited several successful biotechs, including Verona Pharma, which was acquired by Merck for $10 billion, and Carmot Therapeutics, which Roche bought for $2.7 billion.

items.title: Novartis drags peers down with triple asset stumble
items.snippet: Novartis’ shares fell 13% this week after the report of three separate late-stage asset setbacks. The impact went beyond the Swiss drugmaker, dragging peers down across the market.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Novartis’ board faces investor scrutiny after M&A misfires and R&D flops
items.snippet: Back-to-back failures of multiple late-phase trials have raised questions about how Novartis has deployed capital in pursuit of drugs to drive growth through the 2030s.

items.title: Takeda’s long-term R&D head announces exit after major pipeline reorganization
items.snippet: A few months after a new CEO stepped up to helm Takeda, the drugmaker will now have to prepare for another leadership change as its long-time R&D head plans his exit.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.
